**`library/domains/humanities/domains/philosophy/domains/western/domains/metaphysics/texts/state-time-and-event.md`** — 113 lines, one claim: state, time, and event are three aspects of one structure (traces through a state space with Markov-sufficient summaries).

The text covers:
- **Philosophy of time**: McTaggart (A/B-series), Prior (tense logic as modal evaluation at the current state), Whitehead (actual occasions as transitions producing inherited data)
- **Event ontology**: Davidson (causes/effects → predecessor/successor transitions), Kim (property exemplification → state-after)
- **Formal state**: Mealy/Moore machines (state screens off past), Markov property (sufficient summary), coalgebra (Rutten — states as observational equivalence classes)
- **The convergence**: all traditions instantiate the same architecture — states summarize, events transition, time orders
- **State/event distinction**: states persist, events happen, but the distinction is relative to granularity; Bergson's critique (states as cognitive compressions of duration) is compatible with the formal picture
